landmarks.name: Home Island
landmarks.writeup: One of the two inhabited islands, known for its traditional Cocos Malay community and cultural heritage.

wiki.extract: The Cocos (Keeling) Islands, officially the Territory of Cocos (Keeling) Islands, are an Australian external territory located in the Indian Ocean, comprising a small archipelago approximately midway between Australia and Sri Lanka and relatively close to the Indonesian island of Sumatra. The territory's dual name reflects that the islands have historically been known as either the Cocos Islands or the Keeling Islands, the latter of which is still a common short name.

landmarks.name: Direction Island
landmarks.writeup: Famous for its natural beauty, coral reefs, and as a popular spot for snorkeling and diving.

wiki.extract: West Island, part of the South Keeling Islands, is the capital of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, an Australian external territory in the Indian Ocean. The population is roughly 120, making it the third smallest capital in the world, and consists mainly of Europeans. It is less populous than Home Island, the only other inhabited island.

landmarks.name: West Island
landmarks.writeup: The administrative center of the territory, hosting government offices and the airport.

cultural_events.name: Hari Raya Aidilfitri
cultural_events.writeup: A significant Muslim festival celebrated by the Cocos Malay community marking the end of Ramadan.

cultural_events.name: Cocos Islands Day
cultural_events.writeup: An annual event celebrating the unique heritage and history of the islands.

food_writeup: The cuisine of the Cocos (Keeling) Islands reflects a blend of Malay and Australian influences, featuring seafood, coconut-based dishes, and traditional Malay spices.
brief_history: Discovered in 1609, the islands were settled by the Clunies-Ross family in the 19th century who established a coconut plantation economy. The territory became an Australian external territory in 1955.

important_people.name: John Clunies-Ross
important_people.description: Early settler and founder of the Clunies-Ross dynasty on the islands.

important_people.name: Atoll Chief
important_people.description: Traditional leader of the Cocos Malay community.
